pages.text: A permanent, fuel-free heat source that can also supply oxygen.

pages.title: Placement
pages.text: Put it inside a sealed room or in its wall, touching the air. $(danger)Another wall between them blocks heat and oxygen.$()$(br2)Rooms touching it share its output.

pages.name: Core on a Room's Edge
pages.text: Roof left off. The Core sits in the wall, touching the room's air.

pages.title: Depth
pages.text: Below $(bold)Y=0$(): full output.$(br)At Y=0 or above: heat transfer and supply temperature $(danger)halve$().$(br2)Right-click for its interface. See $(l:advanced/core_upgrades)Core Upgrades$(/l).

pages.title: Room Warmth
pages.text: Core heat is stored once in the room's air and walls; walking closer adds nothing.$(br2)A thermostat can't switch it off. If it overshoots, use a $(l:heating/heat_vent)Heat Vent$(/l).

pages.title: Supply Temperature
pages.text: $(bold)50°C$() below Y=0, $(bold)25°C$() at the surface, before upgrades.$(br2)It only heats cooler air and walls; it can't cool them.

pages.title: Oxygen
pages.text: A breach stops its oxygen. Repair every opening and wait about 5 s; EVA covers the gap.$(br2)See $(l:heating/atmospheric_breach)Room Breaches$(/l).

pages.title: Outdoors
pages.text: In open terrain it warms a $(bold)12-block$() field by $(bold)+50°C$() at the default allocation.$(br2)The heat share scales it; the surface penalty applies.
A Frozen Heart in the center with Thermal Cores, diamond blocks and obsidian.$(br2)$(flavor)Expensive? Ask yourself at 3 AM when the heater runs out of coal.$()
